points.why: It says scores are often uncalibrated and need checking, but never says the system's own confidence shouldn't set how much scrutiny a claim gets.
It explains that nobody looks at auto-approved claims, so 'almost no problems' measures detection rather than accuracy.
It recommends a permanent random blind audit stratified by type and dollar amount, plus weighting by stakes, which supplies independent ground truth.
It floats a payout cap for high-value claims whatever the score, but tentatively, and never mentions rule-checkable conditions like policy coverage.

pitfalls.why: It says the clean record can't justify lowering the threshold and makes any change depend on audit error rates.
